sections.label: The Models
paragraphs: Kimi K3 on high effort against Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 on high effort. Both are new to the benchmark, and this is the first game either has played here.

The effort setting cost them very differently. Over the 42 picks of the draft, Muse Spark spent 89,097 reasoning tokens to Kimi's 18,355 — five times as much thinking for a deck that lost. The whole match, draft and game together, came to $1.95.

sections.label: Draft
paragraphs: The models drafted their own decks from an eight-seat pod. Picks and reasoning are [[view:draft|here]], the final lists [[view:decks|here]].

Kimi K3 built Selesnya Allies and earthbend, and said so out loud from early in the draft: white Ally payoffs, green earthbend creatures, and fight-based removal in [[card:Rocky Rebuke]], [[card:Allies at Last]] and [[card:Earth Kingdom Jailer]]. It refused a splash on the grounds that the only off-colour cards in its pool were a Swamp and a dual it did not need.

Muse Spark drafted Rakdos aggro: three [[card:Vindictive Warden]], two [[card:Deadly Precision]], [[card:Azula, On the Hunt]] and [[card:Firebender Ascension]] as an early engine. It is the faster deck on paper, and for four turns it played like it.

rounds.label: Turn 1
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Muse Spark]] takes the play and keeps a seven of four Swamps, [[card:Vindictive Warden]], [[card:Azula, On the Hunt]] and [[card:Firebender Ascension]] — light on spells, but every spell is one it wants.
[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] keeps three lands with [[card:Raucous Audience]], [[card:Rocky Rebuke]], [[card:Earth Kingdom Jailer]] and [[card:Earth Kingdom General]], and plays a Forest.

rounds.label: Turn 2
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Muse Spark]] plays a Mountain and casts [[card:Firebender Ascension]], which makes a 2/2 Soldier token immediately and starts collecting quest counters.
[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] plays a Plains and casts [[card:Haru, Hidden Talent]], explicitly sequencing for next turn: with Haru down, casting an Ally will earthbend a land into a creature.

rounds.label: Turn 3
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Muse Spark]] attacks with the token for 2 and adds [[card:Vindictive Warden]], a 2/3 with menace, postcombat.
[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] declines the block — trading its 1/1 engine for a token is a bad deal — takes 2 down to 18, and casts [[card:Raucous Audience]] postcombat to trigger Haru's earthbend.

rounds.label: Turn 4
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Muse Spark]] attacks with both creatures for 4, pushing [[card:Firebender Ascension]] to three counters, and lands [[card:Azula, On the Hunt]] postcombat. Kimi is on 14 facing a 4/3, a menace creature, a token and a nearly-online enchantment. This is the high-water mark.

[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] casts a second [[card:Raucous Audience]] and then finds the turn: [[card:Allies at Last]] lets two of its creatures deal damage equal to their power, and two 2-power Audiences make exactly 4 — enough to kill the 4/3 Azula before it ever untaps, without trading a creature or touching Haru.

rounds.label: Turn 5
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Muse Spark]] answers in kind. It attacks with the Soldier alone so the Warden cannot be double-blocked, then casts [[card:Deadly Precision]] postcombat, sacrificing the already-tapped token to pay for it, and kills [[card:Haru, Hidden Talent]]. Using a creature that had already attacked is a genuinely tidy piece of sequencing.
[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] casts [[card:Earth Kingdom Jailer]] and exiles the Warden with its enter trigger, which leaves Muse Spark with no creatures at all, then attacks with both Audiences for 4.

rounds.label: Turn 6
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Muse Spark]] casts [[card:Fire Navy Trebuchet]], a 0/4 wall, as a blocker for the Jailer.

[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] casts [[card:Earth Kingdom General]], earthbending a Forest into a hasty 2/2 and gaining 2 life, then attacks with everything. Its notes twice claim the Trebuchet "can't block" because it has defender — which is backwards, defender stops a creature attacking, not blocking. Muse Spark duly blocks the Jailer with it. The misread costs nothing, because attacking wide was right anyway and 4 damage still gets through.

rounds.label: Turn 7
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Muse Spark]] casts [[card:Treetop Freedom Fighters]], which brings an Ally token with it — two more blockers against a board that now outclasses it.

[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] removes one of them first: [[card:Rocky Rebuke]] with the 3/3 Jailer kills the 2/1 Freedom Fighters and the Jailer survives. It then attacks with five creatures for 11; the token chumps, the wall blocks, and 6 gets through. Muse Spark is on 6.

rounds.label: Turn 8
paragraphs: [[player:PilotB|Muse Spark]] plays a Mountain and, facing lethal with one wall, blocks the Jailer again to minimise the damage. Its own note says it plainly: likely dead.
[[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] attacks for lethal and wins on turn 16, at 13 life.

Muse Spark drafted the faster deck and played the better turn 5, and still lost by four turns. Two things did it: [[card:Allies at Last]] answering Azula for one card and no trades, and [[card:Earth Kingdom Jailer]] exiling the Warden a turn later. After that it was a Rakdos aggro deck with no creatures, facing an engine that turns lands into attackers.
